claims.text: The engineered multilayer architecture creates numerous coherent interfaces.
Coherent interfaces impede dislocation motion.
The multilayer architecture suppresses dynamic recovery processes.
Variations in layer lattice parameters and chemistry generate interfacial back stresses.
Interfacial back stresses block creep-related dislocation glide.
Blocking creep-related dislocation glide reduces plastic-strain accumulation under sustained load.
The as-deposited coatings contain coherent, lattice-mismatched interfaces produced by intentional compositional variation between otherwise similar layers.
A multilayer coating and a homogeneous coating can be compared while holding overall composition and total thickness constant.
Testing from room temperature to 600 °C for several hours is expected to produce measurable time-dependent plastic deformation.
Controlled lattice mismatch and differences in layer chemistry and lattice parameters create obstacles to dislocation propagation.
Interfaces between alternating layers act as barriers to dislocation nucleation.
Interface-generated back stresses reduce creep and delay dynamic recovery.
Homogeneous high-entropy-alloy coatings lack the deliberate interfaces responsible for the proposed strengthening mechanism.
Under identical stress and temperature conditions, multilayer coatings will exhibit lower creep strain than homogeneous coatings.
Under identical stress and temperature conditions, multilayer coatings will deform more slowly than homogeneous coatings.
The proposed mechanism requires the interfaces to remain coherent.
The proposed mechanism requires an optimized layer thickness.
Excessively high temperature or interface degradation through interdiffusion may diminish resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation.
The magnitude of deformation resistance depends on layer thickness, lattice mismatch, interface quality, temperature, and stress.
A lack of statistically significant deformation reduction or a lack of evidence for interface-mediated dislocation blocking would reject the hypothesis.
